inputs.userGoal: Deploy SQL Server VMs across two Azure regions behind Private Link Services, accessed by Snowflake via Private Endpoints. Build auto-failover strategy for SQL (WSFC + Always On AG) and cross-region PE access for Snowflake failover scenarios.
subGoals: Production-grade: zone redundancy, private networking only, no public endpoints
DR-ready: WSFC + Always On AG with async cross-region replication, Cloud Witness quorum
Security-first: NSG-restricted subnets, system-assigned managed identity, TLS 1.2 enforced

architecturePrinciples: Highly available — 2 VMs per region across Availability Zones
Disaster recovery — cross-region async AG replication with manual failover
Secure — all SQL access via Private Link only, no public endpoints
Observable — centralized Log Analytics for all resources
Snowflake-integrated — Private Link Services exposed for Snowflake PE provisioning

resources.name: rg-sql-plink-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Resource group for primary region resources. Separate RGs per region enable independent lifecycle management and RBAC scoping.
alternativesConsidered: Single resource group for both regions
reasoning.tradeoffs: Separate RGs add management overhead but improve blast radius isolation for DR.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Top-level container, no dependencies.

resources.name: rg-sql-plink-centralus-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Resource group for secondary/DR region resources.
alternativesConsidered: Single resource group for both regions
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same as primary RG reasoning.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Top-level container, no dependencies.

resources.name: log-sql-plink-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Centralized log aggregation for VM diagnostics, LB metrics, and NSG flow logs across both regions. WAF Operational Excellence pillar.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Single workspace simplifies cross-region correlation but may have minor ingestion latency from Central US.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Deployed in primary region RG.

resources.name: stcloudwitness001

reasoning.whyChosen: Cloud Witness for WSFC quorum. Placed in a third region (East US) to avoid split-brain when either East US 2 or Central US goes down. Standard_LRS is sufficient for the small quorum blob.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Cloud Witness requires outbound HTTPS (443) from VMs to Azure Storage. Minimal cost.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Placed in primary RG for management simplicity. Region is independent (East US).

resources.name: vnet-sql-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Primary region VNet. /16 provides ample address space for SQL VMs, PLS NAT, and future growth.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Large address space is slightly wasteful but avoids re-addressing if workload grows.

resources.dependencyReasoning: VNet must exist in the resource group.

resources.name: snet-sql-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Dedicated subnet for SQL Server VMs and their NICs. /24 supports up to 251 usable IPs.
reasoning.tradeoffs: /24 is larger than needed for 2 VMs but supports scaling.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Subnet is a child of the VNet.

resources.name: snet-pls-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Dedicated NAT subnet for Private Link Service. PLS requires a separate subnet for SNAT. privateLinkServiceNetworkPolicies must be Disabled.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Separate subnet is required by PLS for NAT IP configurations.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Subnet is a child of the VNet.

resources.name: nsg-sql-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: NSG restricts SQL subnet to only required traffic: SQL port 1433 from PLS NAT subnet, AG endpoint 5022, WSFC port 3343, and LB health probe port 59999.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Tight NSG rules may require updates if additional services need access.

resources.dependencyReasoning: NSG must exist before subnet association.

resources.name: nsg-pls-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: NSG for PLS NAT subnet. Allows inbound on SQL port from Private Endpoint connections.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Minimal rules; PLS connection approval provides additional access control.

resources.dependencyReasoning: NSG must exist before subnet association.

resources.name: nic-sql-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: NIC for SQL VM 1. Accelerated networking enabled for lower latency and higher throughput, critical for SQL Server workloads.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Accelerated networking requires compatible VM size (Standard_E4ds_v5 supports it).

resources.dependencyReasoning: NIC references subnet and inherits subnet NSG.

resources.name: nic-sql-eastus2-002

reasoning.whyChosen: NIC for SQL VM 2. Same configuration as VM 1.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same as nic-sql-eastus2-001.

resources.dependencyReasoning: NIC references subnet and inherits subnet NSG.

resources.name: vm-sql-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Memory-optimized E-series VM for SQL Server workloads (4 vCPUs, 32 GB RAM). Zone 1 for zone redundancy within region. SQL Server 2022 Enterprise for AG support.
reasoning.tradeoffs: E4ds_v5 balances cost and performance. Upgrade to E8+ if workload demands more memory.

resources.dependencyReasoning: VM requires NIC and resource group.

resources.name: vm-sql-eastus2-002

reasoning.whyChosen: Second SQL VM in Zone 2 for intra-region HA. Part of the same WSFC cluster and AG.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Cross-zone deployment adds ~1ms latency but provides zone-level fault isolation.

resources.dependencyReasoning: VM requires NIC and resource group.

resources.name: lbi-sql-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Standard Internal LB required for: (1) AG listener IP, (2) Private Link Service backend. Floating IP enabled for AG listener. Health probe on port 59999 detects which VM owns the AG primary replica.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Standard LB required for PLS. Floating IP required for AG listener. DNN would eliminate LB but doesn't support PLS.

resources.dependencyReasoning: LB frontend IP references the SQL subnet.

resources.name: pls-sql-eastus2-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Private Link Service exposes the ILB (AG listener) to Snowflake via Private Endpoints. NAT subnet provides SNAT addresses. Auto-approval disabled for security — connections must be manually approved.
alternativesConsidered: Direct VNet peering to Snowflake (not supported)
reasoning.tradeoffs: PLS adds NAT hop but provides isolation and cross-tenant private connectivity. Max 8 NAT IPs for scaling.

resources.dependencyReasoning: PLS references the ILB frontend IP and uses the PLS NAT subnet for SNAT.

resources.name: vnet-sql-centralus-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Secondary region VNet. Non-overlapping with primary (10.1.0.0/16) to enable VNet peering.
reasoning.tradeoffs: VNet peering is lower latency and higher bandwidth than VPN Gateway.

resources.dependencyReasoning: VNet must exist in the secondary resource group.

resources.name: snet-sql-centralus-001

reasoning.whyChosen: SQL VM subnet in secondary region. Same design as primary.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same as primary.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Subnet is a child of the VNet.

resources.name: snet-pls-centralus-001

reasoning.whyChosen: PLS NAT subnet in secondary region. Same design as primary.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same as primary.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Subnet is a child of the VNet.

resources.name: nsg-sql-centralus-001

properties.securityRules: Same rules as nsg-sql-eastus2-001 with adjusted source CIDR (10.2.2.0/24)

reasoning.whyChosen: NSG for SQL subnet in secondary region. Same security posture as primary.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same as primary.

resources.dependencyReasoning: NSG must exist before subnet association.

resources.name: nsg-pls-centralus-001

reasoning.whyChosen: NSG for PLS NAT subnet in secondary region.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same as primary.

resources.dependencyReasoning: NSG must exist before subnet association.

resources.name: nic-sql-centralus-001

reasoning.whyChosen: NIC for SQL VM 1 in secondary region.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same as primary.

resources.dependencyReasoning: NIC references subnet.

resources.name: nic-sql-centralus-002

reasoning.whyChosen: NIC for SQL VM 2 in secondary region.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same as primary.

resources.dependencyReasoning: NIC references subnet.

resources.name: vm-sql-centralus-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Secondary region SQL VM in Zone 1. Async AG replica for DR.
alternativesConsidered: Smaller VM for cost savings in DR
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same size as primary ensures identical performance after failover.

resources.dependencyReasoning: VM requires NIC and resource group.

resources.name: vm-sql-centralus-002

reasoning.whyChosen: Second SQL VM in secondary region Zone 2. Provides intra-region HA in DR region.
alternativesConsidered: Single VM in DR (lower cost, lower HA)
reasoning.tradeoffs: Two VMs in DR region adds cost but ensures HA even after failover.

resources.dependencyReasoning: VM requires NIC and resource group.

resources.name: lbi-sql-centralus-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Standard Internal LB for AG listener in secondary region. Same configuration as primary.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Standard LB required for PLS. Same tradeoffs as primary.

resources.dependencyReasoning: LB frontend IP references the SQL subnet.

resources.name: pls-sql-centralus-001

reasoning.whyChosen: Private Link Service in secondary region exposes the ILB to Snowflake. Critical for both SQL-failover and Snowflake-failover cross-region access.
reasoning.tradeoffs: PLS in both regions ensures any failover combination works via Private Endpoints.

resources.dependencyReasoning: PLS references the ILB frontend IP and uses the PLS NAT subnet.

resources.name: peer-eastus2-to-centralus

reasoning.whyChosen: Global VNet peering enables WSFC and AG replication traffic between regions. Lower latency and higher bandwidth than VPN Gateway.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Global VNet peering has per-GB data transfer costs. WSFC traffic should be minimal.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Both VNets must exist before peering.

resources.name: peer-centralus-to-eastus2

reasoning.whyChosen: Reciprocal peering from secondary to primary. VNet peering is non-transitive and requires bidirectional configuration.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Same as forward peering.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Both VNets must exist before peering.

overallReasoning.summary: Multi-region SQL Server HA/DR architecture with Private Link Service exposure for Snowflake. Primary region (East US 2) hosts 2 SQL VMs in different availability zones behind an Internal Standard LB with AG listener. Private Link Service fronts the ILB for Snowflake PE access. Secondary region (Central US) mirrors the architecture with async AG replicas. Global VNet peering enables cross-region WSFC/AG traffic. Cloud Witness in a third region (East US) prevents split-brain. Four Snowflake PE connections (2 per PLS) cover all failover combinations.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Cross-region async AG replication means potential data loss (RPO > 0) during unplanned failover. Standard ILB required for PLS adds floating-IP complexity. PLS NAT subnet consumes additional IPs. No Key Vault or CMK included — can be added if encryption requirements warrant it. Snowflake PE provisioning is outside Terraform scope (handled via Snowflake SQL commands).

plan.validation: All 4 SQL VMs reference valid subnets in non-overlapping VNet address spaces. ILBs use Standard SKU required by PLS. PLS NAT subnets have privateLinkServiceNetworkPolicies disabled. VNet peering addresses don't overlap (10.1.0.0/16 vs 10.2.0.0/16). NSGs allow required ports for SQL (1433), AG endpoint (5022), WSFC (3343), and health probes (59999).
